title: Time's Arrow
events_chronological: Odilo Unverdorben grows up in a small German town and qualifies as a doctor.
Odilo marries Herta, and the child they have dies in infancy.
Odilo takes a post at an institute where the disabled are killed by injection and by gas.
Odilo is transferred to a camp in the east and stands beside the senior doctor at selections on the ramp.
Odilo carries out dental work and experiments on prisoners inside the camp.
Odilo takes a prisoner as a lover and has her sent to the chamber when he has finished with her.
The camp is emptied ahead of the advancing army and Odilo walks west carrying false papers.
Odilo hides for years in Portugal under the name Hamilton de Souza, living quietly off gold.
He crosses to New York as John Young, handed a new identity by a churchman who asks him nothing.
Working in American hospitals, he inflicts pain on patients and tells himself he is healing them.
He conducts a long affair with a woman called Irene, who never learns one true thing about him.
He grows old as Tod Friendly, gardening, hoarding tins, and waking from dreams of a man in a white coat.
Tod Friendly collapses in his garden and dies in an American hospital.
syuzhet_notes: The narration runs strictly from the death backwards to the birth, so the doctor appears to be a healer and the camp appears to be a place where people are made. Told-order bullet 1 is the last thing that happens and bullet 13 the first.
fabula_notes: Because the narrator reads every action in reverse, the surface of the prose inverts cause and effect. These bullets record what actually occurred, in the order it occurred.
